thread.title: Stock Market Update: Asia Mixed, Europe Mostly Higher

title: Stock Market Update: Asia Mixed, Europe Mostly Higher
text:
Strong: Communication Services, Consumer Discretionary, Industrials, Energy Weak: Utilities, Information Technology, Financials Moving the Market
Apple (AAPL) extends monthly losses; weighs on the information technology sector
Congresswoman Maxine Waters reportedly issues discouraging regulatory remarks; financials sector underperforms
A rebound in crude oil soothes the oil-sensitive energy sector
Consumer Price Index for October (Briefing.com consensus +0.3%) increases 0.3% as expected Asia Mixed, Europe Mostly Higher 14-Nov-18 08:50 ET Market is Closed
[BRIEFING.COM] S&P futures vs fair value: +18.30. Nasdaq futures vs fair value: +54.30.
The S&P 500 futures have climbed, now trading 18 points, or 0.7%, above fair value.
Equity indices in the Asia-Pacific region ended Wednesday on a mixed note. China reported disappointing Retail Sales for October (+8.6% year-over-year; expected +9.2%) while Japan's Q3 GDP contracted 0.3% quarter-over-quarter, according to the flash reading. In China, National Bureau of Statistics spokeswoman Liu Aihua said that while the Chinese economy is facing many external uncertainties, it remains stable. Low inflation leaves significant room for policy adjustments. Automakers in Japan displayed relative strength amid reports the U.S. will hold off on implementing tariffs on auto imports for now. In economic data: China's October Retail Sales +8.6% year-over-year (expected 9.2%; last 9.2%), October Industrial Production +5.9% year-over-year (expected 5.8%; last 5.8%), and October Fixed Asset Investment +5.7% year-over-year (expected 5.5%; last 5.4%) Japan's Q3 GDP -0.3% quarter-over-quarter, as expected (last 0.8%); -1.2% year-over-year (expected -1.0%; last 3.0%). Q3 GDP Capital Expenditure -0.2% quarter-over-quarter (expected 0.6%; last 3.1%) and Q3 GDP External Demand -0.1% quarter-over-quarter, as expected (last -0.1%). September Industrial Production -0.4% month-over-month (expected -1.1%; last -1.1%) and Tertiary Industry Activity Index -1.1% month-over-month (expected -0.4%; last 0.4%) Australia's Q3 Wage Price Index +0.6% quarter-over-quarter, as expected (last 0.5%); +2.3% year-over-year, as expected (last 2.1%). November Westpac Consumer Sentiment 2.8% (last 1.0%) South Korea's October Unemployment Rate 3.9% (last 4.0%) India's October WPI Inflation +5.28% year-over-year (expected 5.00%; last 5.13%)
---Equity Markets--- Japan's Nikkei added 0.2%. Softbank, SUMCO, TDK, Subaru, Suzuki Motor, Mazda Motor, Konica Minolta, Toyota Motor, Bridgestone, TOTO, and Nissan Motor gained between 1.4% and 4.7%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 0.5% amid losses in roughly half of its components. CNOOC, PetroChina, and China Petrol & Chemical lost between 2.3% and 4.7% while Geely Automobile, Tencent Holdings, AAC Technologies, and BoC Hong Kong surrendered between 0.3% and 1.6%. China's Shanghai Composite ended lower by 0.9%. Eastern Gold Jade, Shandong Hualu Hengsheng Chemical, ENN Ecological Holdings, and Nanjing Textiles Import & Export Corp lost between 4.2% and 5.4%. India's Sensex settled just below its flat line. Sun Pharma slid 7.4% in response to disappointing results while financials like Kotak Mahindra Bank, Yes Bank, and AXIS Bank lost between 1.0% and 3.0%. HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and IndusInd Bank posted gains between 1.5% and 2.0%.
Major European indices trade mostly higher with Italy's MIB (-0.1%) trailing the remaining indices. The Italian government replied to the European Commission's request for a corrected budget, but the main points of the plan have not changed, as Italy continues targeting a budget deficit of 2.4%. Yesterday's response noted that privatization efforts are expected to add one percentage point to GDP while spending on infrastructure maintenance is expected to reach EUR1 billion. The European Commission will issue a response to Italy next week. British Prime Minister Theresa May is expected to hold a cabinet meeting today, during which she will lobby for support for her draft Brexit plan. In economic data: Eurozone flash Q3 GDP +0.2% quarter-over-quarter, as expected (last 0.2%); +1.7% year-over-year, as expected (last 1.7%). Q3 Employment Change +0.2% quarter-over-quarter (expected 0.3%; last 0.4%); +1.3% year-over-year (expected 1.4%; last 1.5%). September Industrial Production -0.3% month-over-month (expected -0.4%; last 1.0%); +0.9% year-over-year (expected 0.3%; last 0.9%) Germany's flash Q3 GDP -0.2% quarter-over-quarter (expected -0.3%; last 0.5%); +1.1% year-over-year (expected 1.3%; last 2.3%) UK's October CPI +0.1% month-over-month (expected 0.2%; last 0.1%); +2.4% year-over-year (expected 2.5%; last 2.4%). October core CPI +1.9% year-over-year, as expected (last 1.9%). October Input PPI +0.8% month-over-month (expected 0.6%; last 1.4%) and Output PPI +0.3% month-over-month (expected 0.2%; last 0.4%). House Price Index +3.5% year-over-year (expected 3.3%; last 3.1%) France's October CPI +0.1% month-over-month (expected 0.1%; last 0.1%); +2.2% year-over-year, as expected (last 2.2%) Spain's October CPI +0.9% month-over-month, as expected (last 0.6%); +2.3% year-over-year, as expected (last 2.3%)
---Equity Markets--- UK's FTSE is up 0.5%. Consumer names like ITV, Paddy Power, Reckitt Benckiser, Kingfisher, British American Tobacco, Next, Marks & Spencer, Taylor Wimpey, Barratt Developments, and Merlin Entertainments sport gains between 1.3% and 5.7%. France's CAC is now up 0.4% with most components in the green. Valeo, Michelin, Peugeot, and Saint Gobain lead the index higher with gains between 1.8% and 4.8%. Germany's DAX has climbed 0.6%. Volkswagen, Daimler, and BMW are up between 2.0% and 3.0%, while Bayer, Thyssenkrupp, Allianz, and Siemens show losses between 0.1% and 1.5%. Italy's MIB trades lower by 0.1%. Banco Bpm, UBI Banca, Bper Banca, Banca Generali, UniCredit, Intesa Sanpaolo, and Banca Mediolanum show losses between 0.1% and 2.3%. Add this to my Page Alerts . MARKET PLACE
